written.description: Rules on whether an agent skill is malicious, with a model judge whose catch and false-positive rates are published against a labelled test set. A team picks a policy and suppresses known findings, so the same skill gets the same verdict on every run.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(ci): run release evidence scans in a network namespace (#280)

* fix(ci): run release evidence scans in a network namespace

The release evidence job blocked all outbound traffic for the runner UID
with iptables while the scans ran. On hosted runners the runner agent runs
as the same user, so it lost its own connection to GitHub, and the job
failed with "The hosted runner lost communication with the server". The
2.2.2, 2.3.0 and 2.3.1 evidence runs each needed several dispatches because
of it.

Run the scan body as the same user in a fresh network namespace instead,
as detection-impact.yml already does. The namespace has only a down
loopback interface, so the scans still cannot open any socket, loopback
included, and the existing isolation check runs inside it. Only an
explicit list of variables, plus UV_*, crosses into the sandbox, and the
credential strip still runs before it.

* fix(ci): drop sudo and docker access inside the scan sandboxes

The scans still ran as the runner user with its passwordless sudo, so a
scan process could nsenter back into the host network namespace.
--init-groups also kept the docker group, and the docker socket is not
network-namespaced. Both sandboxes, release evidence and detection impact,
now run with --clear-groups --no-new-privs, and each fails if sudo still
works inside it. The old iptables rule had the same gap.
